artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a rationally connected smooth complex projective manifold (i.e., any two general points of $X$ can be joined by a rational curve). Assume that the tangent bundle $T_X$ is pseudo-effective in the following sense: there exists an ample line bundle $A$ on $X$ such that, for every integer $m>0$, the sheaf $A\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{m}(T_X)$ is generically globally generated, i.e. its global sections generate the stalk at a general point of $X$. Equivalently, on the projectivized bundle $\mathbb{P}(T_X)$, the non-nef locus of the tautological line bundle $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}(T_X)}(1)$ does not dominate $X$.

Question: Under these hypotheses, must the anti-canonical divisor $-K_X$ be big (i.e., must its Iitaka–Kodaira dimension equal $\dim X$)?
artifact.category_tag: Positivity of tangent bundles in algebraic geometry
artifact.status_search_result: The question is conjectured in work of Hosono–Iwai–Matsumura (2019) and is restated as a problem in subsequent surveys. Searches indicate it remains open in general; partial results exist (e.g., low-dimensional cases, the surface case, and the strongly pseudo-effective setting under further assumptions), but no full proof for arbitrary rationally connected projective manifolds with pseudo-effective tangent bundle has been recorded.

status_evidence.claim: Indicates the conjecture is still treated as open.
